# diyalamp

> A free, open-source Markdown writing app for macOS. A tool for the mind.

## Desktop app

Version 1.1.3 is available for Apple silicon and Intel Macs at https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/tag/v1.1.3. Both DMGs include a runtime; users do not install Java separately. This release is unsigned and not Apple-notarized; macOS may block launch.

The desktop app is light mode only. Its JavaFX workspace uses AtlantaFX CupertinoLight and RichTextFX controls, with a shared top toolbar and user-selectable accent. Body text and controls use bundled static Inter at 16 px, with real regular, italic, semibold, and semibold italic faces. Inline code and code blocks use Menlo at 16 px. Java is an implementation detail, not an account or service dependency.

Open a folder to browse local .md and .markdown files and subfolders. The app supports rendered editing of common Markdown, formatting and slash commands, filename search, closable and reorderable tabs, side-by-side notes, autosave, conflict detection, and recoverable deletion. No account, subscription, server, or AI service is required for writing.

## Connected notes and focus tools

Write [[Note name]] or a relative Markdown file link to connect existing local notes. Wiki links may include a heading or an alias, such as [[Note name#Heading|Label]]. Code, escaped brackets, web links, hidden paths, and symlink or outside-folder destinations do not create graph connections. The inspector uses SmartGraph for a directed diagram in its top third and Incoming and Outgoing lists below it. A link in an origin note is outgoing there and incoming at its target. Open a note from either list or by double-clicking a graph node. The inspector defaults closed; open Connections from the toolbar. It does not create notes or rewrite links.

The index reads saved Markdown in a background worker after safe saves and folder/file operations. It is bounded to 5,000 notes, 30,000 traversed entries, 1 MiB of content per note, and 32 MiB total content per scan. Skipped files or scan limits produce a partial-index notice. The diagram draws up to 60 notes; the lists retain every indexed connection for the active note. This is a local note-link inspector, not Obsidian plugin compatibility or an unbounded knowledge-graph service.

Zen mode hides workspace controls without closing notes. The top-toolbar Pomodoro control opens an animated AtlantaFX Popover with Start, Stop, and Reset.

Updates are explicit: Help → Check for updates checks for a newer stable release but does not download it. A user can choose to download the update, then choose Install and Restart. The app checks the download against the published SHA-256 checksum, validates the staged app, and saves notes before installation. A save conflict cancels installation. Checksums are download-integrity checks; the release remains unsigned and not Apple-notarized.

## Browser notebook

The website and its separate browser notebook retain a dark interface with self-hosted Inter. The browser notebook is a demonstration, not a screenshot of the light desktop app. Browser notes live in browser storage, which can be cleared; export important writing. Desktop and browser notes are not automatically synced, and the browser notebook does not reproduce every desktop control.

## Scope and alternatives

diyalamp is a focused personal-writing alternative to tools such as Notion and Typora. It does not replace Notion's team databases, Coda's automations, or Obsidian's plugin ecosystem. Cloud services and publication integrations are outside this desktop release. Do not infer that comparison apps are affiliated with diyalamp.

## Size budget

Under 5 MB installed is an aspirational target, not an achieved size. The self-contained app includes its runtime and UI libraries. Download size and installed size are different measurements; do not reuse figures from an older release. Do not describe diyalamp as currently installing in less than 5 MB or 10 MB. Version 1.1.3 DMG downloads are 48,033,713 bytes for Apple silicon (48.0 MB) and 49,514,944 bytes for Intel (49.5 MB), using decimal MB. Matching SHA-256 files accompany both DMGs.
